title: Allocation address reuse does not restore the old object's lifetime
summary: After deallocation, another allocation creates a new object even at the same address. Views of the old allocation need a separate validity check.
applies: C11; Offline memory diagnostics and object representation
detail: When reviewing the tracking log, record the allocation event together with the address as the object identifier; the subview inherits the ownership of the parent view. C11 §6.2.4 and §7.22.3 define objects and allocate storage periods.
boundary: The generation number in the log is tracker metadata; plain C pointers themselves don't carry it.
relevance: Distinguish between "the numerical address is still in a piece of live memory" and "this access belongs to the original object".
